title: Title-quality check before analyze/save-suggest
description:
Bookmark titles are the strongest signal Jev receives today (URL + title + domain only). Generic titles ('Untitled', 'Home', 'Redirecting...', raw UI strings) degrade every question set and waste paid requests. A local, zero-egress title-quality check should run before analyze/save-suggest and either skip or flag low-quality titles.

Scope sketch (from the track plan):
- Pure heuristic in src/decisions/ (no network): too short, all-numeric/symbol junk, matches common noise patterns (Untitled/Home/Login/Index of...), title equals the domain registrable name.
- Behavior: a scan/analyze pre-filter with a reason (like the existing blocklisted skip: {sent:false, reason:'low_quality_title'}), surfaced in the UI as a review-hint rather than silently dropped; user can still force-analyze from the row menu.
- Unit tests over a noise-title corpus; e2e assertion that a low-quality title makes no request.
design: Files: src/decisions/title-quality.ts + tests; wire into src/decisions/pipeline.ts pre-minimize and the scan runner.
acceptance_criteria: Low-quality titles are detected locally with zero egress; the skip reason is visible to the user; forced analyze still works; covered by unit + e2e tests.

title: Opt-in page-text extraction for richer Jev analyze input
description:
Jev analyze currently judges only minimized bookmark metadata (title, cleaned URL, domain). PROJECT_PLAN.md contemplates optional page-text extraction to enrich categorize/tags/misfiled questions. Deferred by design: it needs new permissions and consent, not just code.

Scope sketch (from the track plan):
- A content script injected on explicit user action (never automatically) via the scripting API — adds the scripting permission + a dedicated disclosure.
- Readability (@mozilla/readability) to distill the page body; a hard cap on extracted length (align with the token budget guards in src/jev/budget.ts).
- A separate page-text consent scope following the CONSENT_VERSION pattern in src/consent/ — page text is strictly more sensitive than metadata, so its own grant, its own disclosure string, and its own egress boundary in the DecisionState schema (src/schemas/decision-state.ts) with the same strict-parse gate treatment.
- Minimization stays: extraction happens on-device, only the distilled text (never notes, never full DOM) may enter state fields that the jev_decisions gate strict-parses.
design: Files: likely src/extract/ (content script + distill), src/schemas/decision-state.ts (optional pageText field), src/consent/ (new scope), store/permissions.md. Coordinate with BookmarksManager-f7c lifecycle leak if page-text decisions accumulate.
acceptance_criteria: User can opt in to page-text extraction per disclosure; extracted text is length-capped, consent-gated, visible in the Data sent log, and covered by zero-egress tests when not granted; no new permission is requested before the opt-in flow runs.
